The response correctly identifies tidal locking as the reason we see only one face of the Moon, and the 27.3-day figure is accurate. The explanation of how it happened is broadly right: Earth's gravity raised a tidal bulge, and friction slowed the Moon's spin until the rotation matched its orbit. It is somewhat loose about the mechanism, since the bulge's offset from the Earth-Moon line is what produces the braking torque, but the core reasoning is there. The libration point (about 59% of the surface visible over time) and the note about the far side getting sunlight are accurate and useful additions. Clarity is good. The main flaw is the length constraint: my count is exactly 120 words, which fails "under 120" by a hair.

Score: 7
